captures.description: SHELF-ORDER HERMENEUTICS: the AI Overview gives the study of how a shelf's arrangement 'communicate[s] implicit meaning, shape[s] canonical formation' — #1420's 'A shelf asserts what belongs with what, what precedes what, and what is peripheral' — with Library of Congress shelving as canonical shaping, and offers 'the theoretical paper by Lee Sharks'. #1420's seated text opens as that essay and continues as the Apocalypse-dating article whose title the registry carries.

atoms.evidence: look into the theoretical paper by Lee Sharks on the material argument of collections

inversions.span: Shelf-order hermeneutics is the study of how the physical arrangement, proximity, and sequencing of books on a shelf communicate implicit meaning, shape canonical formation, and guide interpretation.
inversions.against: the essay's purpose of marking the supply: the canon's order (the Apocalypse's terminal place) read as an argument, not a datum about its date; the claim is carried as a generic 'material hermeneutics of collections' (the inversion guidance)
